title: The Real Ghostbusters
build: OUG disk crack, both trainers declined

records.c: The LEVELK stream expands to $FF through $63FF. The picture copy at $C04D overwrites these bytes in the VIC bitmap area.

The first bitmap destination page still holds the fill expanded from LEVELK. Beginning here and ending at $63FF, the remaining bytes of the four-page block are all $FF and will be overwritten by the bitmap copy.

The four-page screen attribute source for $C075. The VIC uses the two nibbles in each visible cell as bitmap colours.
The four-page colour RAM source for $C079. The copy writes $D800-$DBFF to supply the per-cell colour nibble.
Header slot read by the resident actor table selector at $19A2 and $19A9. LEVELK supplies $C0E2 in this slot.
High byte of the actor descriptor base slot. LEVELK sets it to the page of its no-op callback at $C0E2.
The resident code at $1517 reads this word and dispatches to $C011 through $15EB.
High byte of the ending setup callback address, read at $151C.
The ordinary stage object list slot is $C0E2 in LEVELK. The ending callback returns with carry clear, so the resident setup does not process a stage object list.
High byte of the ordinary stage object-list slot. The $C011 callback returns with carry clear and bypasses that ordinary stage setup.
First ordinary stage background slot in the common header. The ending setup takes its display attributes from the bitmap's colour data.
Second ordinary stage background slot. The ending's IRQ does not copy this field to $D023.
Header field tested by the resident stage-zero selection path at $32DB. LEVELK supplies $0B.
Common tile-patch address slot holds $C0E2 in the ending. The setup path draws a complete bitmap and returns with carry clear before the engine stamps map patches.
High byte of the tile-patch address slot in the common header. In LEVELK the complete slot points to the RTS at $C0E2.
The ordinary stage parameter byte is $00 in LEVELK. The ending callback avoids the normal stage parameter load at $1573.
The partner-respawn probe at $1D40 reads this common header slot in play. It is $00 in LEVELK.
The resident loop at $0965 reads this word and dispatches to $C0E2 through $15EB.
High byte of the ordinary update callback address, read by the resident loop at $096A.
Disable interrupts while installing the ending's IRQ at $C0E3 for raster line $FC. Reconfigure VIC control, resume interrupts and disable sprites before copying the picture.
Copy 32 pages of bitmap image data from $9800-$B7FF into VIC RAM at $6000-$7FFF. Start Y at zero and increment the source and destination high bytes each page.
Transfer one page from ($0C),Y to ($0A),Y. The Y wrap ends the page and the X countdown ends the full transfer.
Set up the four-page copy from $B800 to screen RAM at $4000 and from $BC00 to colour RAM at $D800.
Copy one screen attribute and one colour byte per iteration. Increment all four pointer high bytes on Y wrap and decrement the page count.
Select sound bank 3 through $EF8C and switch the VIC to bitmap mode. With $D018 = $08 in VIC bank $4000, the screen remains at $4000 and the bitmap starts at $6000.
Select all keyboard rows at $DC00 and read $DC01 until it returns $FF, so keys carried over from the stage cannot dismiss the ending.
Poll CIA1 port B with all rows selected until at least one bit reads low.
Wait for CIA1 port B to be all ones again after the ending key press. Then restore the resident raster IRQ.
Restore $0A57 as the line-$FC IRQ target, call $2DBE, mark $12 as $FF and return with carry clear.
Return immediately. LEVELK supplies this RTS as its ordinary stage update callback.
Acknowledge VIC and CIA1 interrupt state, save X and Y, increment the resident frame counter in $2D and keep this handler at line $FC.
Set the sound tick flag $50 and call the resident sound engine at $F0D2. Restore Y, X and A and return from interrupt.
